disclaimer: Research compilation, not tax advice. Percentages and caps come from the Income Tax Ordinance (consolidated text as mirrored on Hebrew Wikisource), regulations on the same site, the Tax Authority's 4 Dec 2025 small-business notice, and secondary sources where marked. Amounts annotated by year in the regulations were not cross-checked in Reshumot; verify against the Tax Authority's latest publication or an accountant before filing. Fields in an 'unverified' array could not be confirmed from a primary source.

businessTypeNotes.patur: Income-tax percentages apply to the gross amount paid; vatPct is always 0 (no input VAT, VAT Law s.41).
businessTypeNotes.zair: On the deemed-30% track none of the per-expense income-tax percentages apply (s.87ד): taxable income = 70% of turnover; only keren hishtalmut (17(5א)), pension s.47 and credits remain. 'zair' is a tax-file status, orthogonal to patur/murshe: a murshe can also be zair, and keeps input VAT.
businessTypeNotes.murshe: Income-tax percentages apply; vatPct is the share of the VAT on the invoice that can be reclaimed.
businessTypeNotes.ltd: Same expense percentages; owner-benefit items (car, phone) become salary benefits; companies pay a 45% advance on 'excess expenses' (the non-deductible part of refreshments, gifts, clothing, mobile, car, travel) - Efraty §5.1.4.

conventions.vatPct: percent of the input VAT shown on a valid tax invoice that is reclaimable; null = not determined from a primary source, treat as not reclaimable until verified
conventions.incomeTaxPct: percent of the expense that is deductible; null = depends on a business-use share (see 'basis')
conventions.cap.kind: how to read the cap (max_deduction, max_non_deductible, threshold, per_night_cap, ...)
conventions.values: per-year numeric parameters for the engine; the 2025 and 2026 columns are the tax-year amounts
conventions.tags_default: personal = default tag suggestion should not be business

label.en: Light refreshments at the place of business

conditions: Consumed AT the taxpayer's place of business (מקום העיסוק), not in a café/restaurant/outside
Hot/cold drinks, cookies, fruit and similar only
Visitors or staff (BSH cites Circular 14/2000 for both; not verified at source)
evidence: חשבונית מס / tax invoice in the business's name (osek murshe supplier) or receipt (osek patur supplier: income tax only, no VAT) itemised (supermarket receipt is fine, in business name if you want VAT)
Keep purchase receipts; no attendee list is required by the regulation for light refreshments

sources.title: BSH CPA: כיבודים במקום העסק והוצאות אירוח (secondary)

rules.notes: 80% of the cost is deductible; the other 20% is permanently non-deductible. 'Light refreshments' = cold or hot drinks, cookies and the like (ITA notice 2018, per BSH: seasonal fruit and vegetables count). Meals, catering trays, restaurant food are NOT light refreshments (see il.hosting-il). VAT: the secondary sources conflict (some say input VAT on office coffee/cookies is reclaimable, some say not); VAT reg. 16 bars input VAT on 'hosting' (אירוח) and no primary text says whether staff-kitchen refreshments are hosting. Kept null = do not reclaim by default. Companies/NPOs pay a 45%/90% advance on the non-deductible 'excess expenses' (Efraty §5.1.4).

sources.title: תקנות מס הכנסה (ניכוי הוצאות רכב), התשנ"ה-1995
תקנות מס הכנסה (שווי השימוש ברכב), התשמ"ז-1987

rules.notes: Income tax: deductible = MAX(45% x costs, costs - annual shovi) where shovi = months of use x monthly shovi (price x ~2.48% typical; rate depends on the model's 2010 weighted-price bracket). Price used for shovi is capped (2024: 563,790; 2025: 583,100; 2026: 596,860 per the Wikisource annotation; Efraty's 563,790 'for 2025' is the 2024 figure). 'Costs' = licensing, compulsory + comprehensive insurance, rent/lease, fuel, oil, repairs/maintenance, parking not at/near the place of business, tolls (אגרה) and depreciation (s.21). Applies to M1/N1 vehicles under 3,500 kg; motorcycle L3 = max(costs - shovi, 25%); taxi/bus M1 = 90%; tour/desert vehicle = 80%; driving-school car = 77.5% (68% in the stated case). VAT: purchase VAT is not reclaimable on a private car (reg. 14, il.vehicle.purchase); input VAT on RUNNING costs is reclaimed at 2/3 where the car is mainly for business, 1/4 where mainly private (reg. 18(ב)(2)-(3)) unless the VAT director fixed another split. Non-reclaimed VAT is part of the cost base for the 45%. The deemed-30% zair track ignores all this. Company car (ltd): the company deducts 100% and the employee is taxed on shovi (reg. 3-4).
unverified: depreciation cost ceiling (if any) on expensive cars
cap year-by-year values from an annotated consolidation, not the Reshumot

conditions: Plan/device in the taxpayer's name or business
Not available when the deemed-30% zair track is used
evidence: חשבונית מס / tax invoice in the business's name (osek murshe supplier) or receipt (osek patur supplier: income tax only, no VAT) for the plan and the device
rules.notes: NOT deductible = the lower of 50% of the cost or ₪1,380 a year (₪115/month). So deductible = cost - min(50% x cost, 1,380): 50% when annual cost <= 2,760, otherwise cost - 1,380. The ₪1,380 figure applies to 2023-2027 (earlier years: ₪1,260; the '₪1,200' circulating is stale). The 50%/₪1,380 rule is a 'cap on the disallowed part', not a cap on the deduction. VAT: mixed-use default 2/3 under VAT reg. 18(ב)(2) (practice for phones; the VAT director may fix another ratio).

conditions: Home must be the main place of the business
International calls need a per-call log
evidence: Bezeq/ISP invoices
Call log for international calls
rules.notes: Non-mobile phone at the home is NOT deductible unless the home is where most of the business is run (proved to the assessor). If proved: cost <= ₪26,600 a year -> deduct the lower of 80% x cost and (cost - ₪2,700); cost > ₪26,600 -> deduct cost - ₪5,300 (amounts apply 2024-2027). Calls abroad made in producing income are deductible in full with a call log (date, time, destination, recipient, length, subject, estimated price) even if the home is not the main office.

conditions: Defensible business-use share (document the method)

rules.notes: No dedicated regulation. sources.title: תקנות מס הכנסה (ניכוי הוצאות מסויימות)
sources.section: תקנה 2ב (טלפון בבית) – the only home-office regulation

rules.notes: No regulation or primary ITA instruction fixes a percentage. Practice: apportion by dedicated area or rooms (business rooms / total rooms; a dedicated room typically supports 1/4-1/3). Mortgage INTEREST (not principal) may be apportioned; some practitioners claim 80% of the business share (single opinion, unverified). Purchase VAT on the dwelling is not reclaimable if it also serves as the business place (VAT reg. 15). Costs with VAT (electricity, water) are reclaimed in the business share (reg. 18). Capital-gains/betterment exemption on a later sale may be partly lost for the business portion (flag, unverified). If rented, make sure the lease allows business use and the landlord reports the rent.

rules.notes: Economy: 100% of the fare. Business or first class: 100% of the price of a business-class ticket on the same flight (the excess is non-deductible). VAT: international flights carry 0% VAT, so there is nothing to reclaim. A trip counts only if the trip AND the stay were NECESSARY for producing the income (reg. 2(2) opening words).

label.en: Business trip abroad: hotel / lodging per night

sources.title: Technion HR summary of the ITA travel-abroad amounts at 1.1.2026 (secondary)

rules.notes: Per night, trip of up to 90 nights: first 7 nights deductible up to actual or the cap ($355 in 2025, $365 in 2026). Nights 8-90: a night costing up to $156 (2025) / $160 (2026) is fully deductible; a dearer night is deductible at 75% of the cost but not less than $156/$160 and not more than $266.25 (2025) / ~$274 (2026). Trip over 90 nights: every night capped at $156/$160. Two or more trips with fewer than 14 consecutive days in Israel between them count as one trip. In the listed countries (Australia, Austria, Italy, Iceland, Ireland, Angola, Belgium, Germany, Dubai, Denmark, Netherlands, Hong Kong, UK, Taiwan, Greece, Japan, Luxembourg, Norway, Spain, Oman, Finland, France, Qatar, Korea, Cameroon, Canada, Sweden, Switzerland) the lodging and 'other expenses' limits are raised by 25% (ITA determination 2005). The cap is per night per room, not per person: a double room shared with a non-business companion is deductible only up to the single-room price. Amounts are re-indexed on 1 Jan each year to US CPI. VAT: foreign hotels charge no Israeli VAT.
unverified: 2025 values rest on the Wikisource annotation (2026 values are cross-checked with the Technion summary of the ITA table)

sources.section: תקנה 2(2) – הנסיעה והשהייה הכרחיות לייצור ההכנסה

rules.notes: Popular belief ('it's a business trip so my partner's flight and room are deductible too') is wrong as a default. A companion's flight, extra hotel cost, meals and tours are private (s.32(1)-(2): not wholly and exclusively for producing income). Deductible only if the companion has a genuine, documented business role that required presence (an employee or business partner doing real work, an interpreter, etc.) - then his/her costs are the business's ordinary costs within the same per-night/per-day caps. Shared hotel room: deduct no more than the single-room price. Joint business of spouses (s.66(ד)): each spouse's personal exertion must be required - only then is a spouse's own trip a business trip. I found no ITA circular or Israeli ruling specifically on accompanying partners, so this is the statute applied to the facts, not a published safe harbour.

conditions: Main purpose business
Per-night / per-day caps still apply to business days
evidence: Agenda, invitations, meeting confirmations with dates
Return ticket dates vs the last business day
rules.notes: Only the days of stay that were NECESSARY for the business are covered by lodging and per-diem. Vacation days are personal: lodging, per-diem, rental car and local costs for those days are non-deductible. Flights: practice is that a ticket is fully deductible when the trip's main purpose is business and the vacation is incidental, and apportioned by days (or limited to the business itinerary fare) when the trip is mainly leisure; I found no published ITA rule for the split. A weekend that falls between business days is normally accepted as part of the stay. Keep the evidence that the dates were driven by business meetings.

label.en: Gifts to clients, suppliers and employees (personal event)

conditions: Business relationship (customer/supplier) or an employee's personal event
Track cumulative total per recipient per tax year
evidence: Record: recipient's identifying details, place the gift was given, receipts to verify (reg. 2(4))
Tax invoice for the purchase
rules.notes: Deductible up to ₪240 per person per year for gifts given in Israel (₪230 for 2023, ₪240 for 2024-2027 per the annotated regulation; Efraty's 2025 guide still says ₪230 - flag), and US$15 per person per year for gifts given abroad. The amount above the cap is not deductible. Per-person accumulation across all gifts in the year. VAT: no primary text found on input VAT for client gifts - null. Companies/NPOs pay the 45%/90% advance on the non-deductible excess. Employee gifts above the benefit thresholds are a taxable benefit instead (separate payroll rule).

conditions: Approved institution (סעיף 46)
Total in year above ₪207
Credit cannot exceed tax
evidence: Official s.46 donation receipt (קבלה לפי סעיף 46) with the donor's ID
rules.notes: A donation to an approved institution gives a TAX CREDIT of 35% of the donation (individual; companies use the s.126 rate) if the year's total exceeds ₪207 (2024-2027). The credited base is capped at the lower of 30% of taxable income and ₪10,354,816; excess carries over three years. Combined with R&D deduction the s.46א cap is 50% of taxable income. It is not an expense; do not subtract it from business profit. Only receipts under s.46 from institutions approved for it count.

rules.notes: Fixed assets are deducted over their life, not when bought (straight-line at the regulation rate, from the year put to use). Rates: personal computers 33%, other computers 25%, electronic and computerised equipment 15%, general furniture 6%, private car M1/N1 15%. Not applicable under the deemed-30% zair track, and the depreciation is added back to the sale value for capital-gain purposes (s.87ד(ב)). label.he: רואה חשבון, הנהלת חשבונות, עורך דין, יועץ

conditions: Business purpose; apportion personal work
evidence: חשבונית מס / tax invoice in the business's name (osek murshe supplier) or receipt (osek patur supplier: income tax only, no VAT) with the service description
rules.notes: Fees for running or defending the business are deductible with VAT reclaimable on a tax invoice. Fees for purely personal matters (divorce, personal estate, a private return's personal part) are not; apportion a combined invoice. An osek patur's accountant VAT is a cost (no reclaim).

label.en: Business insurance (liability, professional indemnity, equipment, office)

conditions: Insures the business, not the person
evidence: Policy and premium receipt
rules.notes: Premiums for insuring the business are ordinary expenses. Insurance premiums carry no VAT (financial services), so no input VAT. Personal health, life, car-private-part or home contents are not business insurance.

conditions: Premium paid in the tax year
Shared 5% ceiling with pension credit
evidence: Annual insurer certificate
rules.notes: Not a business expense. Credit of 25% of life-insurance premiums (self, spouse; child over 18 for a 'beneficiary member'), inside a shared ceiling of 5% of qualifying income (for a self-employed person with no employment income) that also covers pension survivors' insurance and the credit on pension deposits. Minimum floor ₪2,268 (2024-2027) where income is low.
unverified: exact combined-ceiling arithmetic when pension credit is also used

conditions: Preferred insurance definition met
evidence: Insurer annual certificate

rules.notes: Deduction up to 3.5% of business income for a 'preferred insurance' (policy to at least age 60 and pays until recovery or age 60). Income ceiling for the 3.5%: the statute ties it to the average wage divided by 4.8 and I could not reproduce the repo's playbook figures (income ceiling ₪356,100, max ₪12,463 for 2025) from the text. Not available in the deemed-30% zair track (s.87ד excludes ss.17-27, and this deduction sits in the s.32(14) family - flag).

conditions: Deposit paid in the tax year
Allowed in the zair track (s.47 is outside ss.17-27)
Beneficiary-member threshold for the higher deduction
evidence: Annual fund certificate (אישור שנתי) for deposits
rules.notes: Deduction (s.47): for a beneficiary member (deposits >= 16% of the average wage: ₪24,069 in 2025, ₪26,436 in 2026) up to 11% of self-employed income up to the first ₪116,400, plus 7% (and an extra 4% on the part of deposits above 12%) of the next band of income, i.e. a combined practical maximum of about 11% of income up to ₪232,800 = ₪25,608. Credit (s.45א(ב), (ה)): 35% on deposits up to 5% of income up to ₪232,800 (about ₪11,640 base -> ₪4,074 credit), on deposits that were not deducted. The ₪116,400 / ₪164,400 statutory amounts are fixed for 2024-2027, so 2025 and 2026 are identical. My reading of the nested definitions matches the repo model (11% deduct + 5% credit within ₪232,800) but the text is intricate - verify with an accountant. The mandatory minimum deposit for the self-employed (4.45% / 12.55%) is a separate pension-extension-order rule in the repo tables.
unverified: exact stacking of 11%/7%/4% bands and the credit base

label.en: Osek zair: 30% deemed expenses instead of actual

conditions: No employees
Accepted books (ניהול פנקסים תקין)
All business income from personal exertion
No part of business income from your employer
No transparent-entity attribution
No more than 25% of business income from a relative or from someone who employed you in the last 3 years
Not a controlling shareholder of a closely held company; not a partner in a partnership; not a kibbutz member
Do tax coordination each year by 25 Dec
evidence: Books (חשבוניות/קבלות) are still required; receipts are not attached to the short report but bookkeeping duty remains and is a condition (BRIT CPA)
Turnover record by month

sources.title: רשות המסים, הודעה 2025-000092 מיום 4.12.2025: רפורמה במיסוי עסקים זעירים
BRIT CPA: רפורמת בעל עסק זעיר (secondary, reproduces ITA circular text)

rules.notes: The reform is NOT new in 2026: it started with tax year 2024. A 'small business owner' (individual resident) with turnover up to the VAT 'osek patur' ceiling (₪120,000 in 2024-2025, ₪122,833 in 2026) deducts a flat 30% of turnover INSTEAD of actual expenses (s.87ד: ss.17-27 do not apply, except s.17(5א) keren hishtalmut; s.47א BL deduction does not apply). Taxable income = 70% of turnover. Pension s.47 and the s.45א credits and personal credit points remain. Losses cannot be carried forward. Turnover includes war indirect-damage compensation; reserve pay and maternity benefits from BL are excluded from the ceiling and get no 30%. Over the ceiling (counting compensation) -> full annual return, and the 30% applies only to the small-business income (ITA notice Dec 2025). Registration is voluntary for a murshe, automatic for a new/existing patur; zair is NOT the same as patur (a murshe can be zair). Tax coordination (תיאום מס) must be done during the year (deadline 25 Dec; 2025 deadline could not be extended); the short report is filed after year-end: for 2024 by 31.07.2025; for 2025 by 31.08.2026 (kolzchut; a search snippet cites 31.05.2026 for 2025 - conflict); from 2026 by 31 March. An ITA proposal to widen short-report eligibility to ₪300,000 turnover is mentioned by Efraty; not enacted as far as found.
unverified: Circular number '78/2024' (as printed on britcpa) not checked at the ITA
BL liability computation for zair (separate BL rules)

conditions: Turnover under the ceiling
Not a mandatory-murshe profession
evidence: Receipts (קבלה) issued, not tax invoices

sources.title: חוק מס ערך מוסף, התשל"ו-1975
sources.section: סעיף 41 – אין ניכוי תשומות אלא לעסקה חייבת

rules.notes: An osek patur charges no VAT and may NOT deduct input VAT (s.41): VAT paid on every purchase is simply part of the expense cost (still deductible for income tax at the rule's percentage on the gross amount). Ceiling: ₪120,000 (2024-2025), ₪122,833 (2026); some professions (lawyers, accountants, doctors, engineers, etc.) must register as murshe regardless. VAT rate 18%. Switching to murshe pays off mainly with large VAT-bearing purchases and mostly-business clients (they reclaim the VAT you charge); with consumer customers you either cut your price by 18/118 or lose margin. Export of services is 0% and keeps input VAT recoverable.

label.en: Record-keeping and evidence rules (what counts as acceptable)

conditions: Invoice in the business's name/ID, with VAT number, date, description, amount
Allocation number when above the threshold
Claim input VAT within 6 months
evidence: Original or digital copy retained (7-year retention is the usual rule; not verified in the bookkeeping regulations here)
rules.notes: VAT input is deductible only with a tax invoice issued properly in the taxpayer's name, claimed within 6 months of its date (s.38(א)). For an invoice over the threshold (before VAT), a Tax Authority allocation number is required or input VAT is denied: ₪20,000 in 2025 (per the repo playbook), ₪10,000 from 1 Jan 2026, ₪5,000 from 1 Jun 2026 (s.38(א1)). Efraty also reports that the expense itself is disallowed when input VAT is lost for lack of an allocation number - I could not find that text in the consolidated Ordinance; treat as likely but unverified. Payments made in breach of the cash-use law and penalised are non-deductible (s.32(16א)) and lose VAT (s.38(א2)); do not rely on cash for large business payments (business cash cap ₪6,000 per the Schedule, unverified for 2026). A receipt (קבלה) from a patur supplier supports the income-tax deduction but carries no VAT. A חשבונית עסקה / proforma is not a tax invoice. Cards, transfers, bit/paybox are fine; keep the statement as a cross-check.
unverified: expense-disallowance consequence of a missing allocation number

title.en: Compare the 30% deemed track with actual expenses
title.he: להשוות מסלול זעיר (30%) מול הוצאות בפועל

moves.when: Turnover <= zair ceiling (122,833 in 2026) and the business qualifies (no employees, personal-exertion income, etc.).
moves.effect: Compute tax twice with ilPlan: zair: taxable = 0.7 x turnover, no 47א BL deduction; actual: taxable = turnover - deductible expenses (apply this table's percentages) - 52% x BL. Actual wins roughly when deductible expenses (after the 80%/45%/50% haircuts) exceed ~30% of turnover MINUS the value of the 52% BL deduction (about 0.52 x BL, which is worth up to ~1.5-6% of profit). Zair also removes the annual return and advances (value of time) and the audit surface; actual keeps loss carry-forward and depreciation. Keep every receipt anyway: if turnover crosses the ceiling the whole year reverts to the regular file.

sources.title: רשות המסים, הודעה 2025-000092 מיום 4.12.2025: רפורמה במיסוי עסקים זעירים

title.en: Keep receipts even on the zair track

moves.when: Any zair whose turnover might exceed the ceiling (including war compensation) or who might be removed from the track.
moves.effect: If registration is cancelled (s.87ג(ג)) you file a full return and need actual-expense proof; the app should flag turnover at 85% of the ceiling.

sources.title: רשות המסים, הודעה 2025-000092 מיום 4.12.2025: רפורמה במיסוי עסקים זעירים

title.en: Switch osek patur to murshe when VAT-bearing costs are large

moves.when: Customers are mostly VAT-registered businesses or foreign (0% VAT), and annual VAT-bearing purchases are large (equipment, car running costs share, rent).
moves.effect: Extra deduction = VAT in business-related purchases x reclaim ratio (100% for equipment/software; 66.7% for mixed car/phone costs; 0% for hosting). Cost: VAT paperwork, price pressure with consumers (price falls by 18/118 if consumers can't recover), bookkeeping ~₪6,500/yr (repo costs).

title.en: Buy coffee/snacks for the office instead of paying in cafés

moves.when: Recurring café spend on a taxpayer who has a real place of business (home office counts only if it is the main place).
moves.effect: Office supplies earn 80% deduction; café coffee earns 0%. Saving = 0.8 x spend x marginal rate (plus the VAT question). Does not help at a café; only supplies consumed at the business place qualify.

title.en: Spread gifts across recipients, track the ₪240 per person per year

moves.effect: Deduct min(240, gifts to person); the rest is lost. Track recipient identity, place and receipts. Prefer many small gifts to a few large ones.

title.en: Document business trips and split private days/companions on separate invoices

moves.when: Any trip abroad with business meetings.
moves.effect: Deductible = flights (economy/business-class-fare cap) + nights within the cap + per-diem for necessary days + rental car cap. Make sure the companion's private costs are paid and invoiced separately; for a shared room deduct the single-room price. App should compute: sum(min(actual, cap) per night) + days x per-diem.

sources.title: Technion HR summary of the ITA travel-abroad amounts at 1.1.2026 (secondary)

title.en: Deposit to pension to the optimum (deduct + credit)

moves.when: Self-employed with taxable profit and room under the ceiling; before 31 Dec.
moves.effect: Best deposit ≈ 16% of min(profit, 232,800): 11% deducted, up to 5% earns a 35% credit; the playbook (il-pension-self-employed-47) already runs this through ilPlan. Beneficiary-member threshold (₪26,436 in 2026) must be met for the full deduction.

moves.when: Self-employed (including zair) with profit; before 31 Dec.
moves.effect: Deduction = min(deposit, 4.5% x min(income, 293,397)) = up to ₪13,202; saving = deduction x marginal rate. Works even on the zair track.

title.en: Time donations to use the 35% credit

moves.effect: Credit = 35% x min(donations, 30% x taxable income, 10,354,816), capped at tax due; carry the excess 3 years. Not a deduction: it saves 35 agorot per shekel, so it is a net cost, not a tax-saver.

title.en: Buy and start using equipment before year-end (depreciation) and reclaim VAT

moves.when: Planned equipment purchase and taxable profit in the current year (murshe).
moves.effect: VAT reclaimed in full in the period; depreciation starts the year put to use at the table rate (33% computers). On the zair track no depreciation.

title.en: Odometer readings 1 Jan and 31 Dec, vehicle log

moves.effect: Without the start/end odometer in the annual return the vehicle expenses are not allowed (reg. 6). Compare 45% to costs - shovi: for expensive cars shovi is high and 45% usually wins; for cheap cars with high costs, costs - shovi may win.

title.en: Ask suppliers for an allocation number on invoices over the threshold

moves.when: Any single invoice above ₪5,000 before VAT from 1 Jun 2026 (₪10,000 in Jan-May 2026; ₪20,000 in 2025).
moves.effect: Without it the input VAT is lost (and reportedly the expense). Flag missing allocation numbers when a receipt above the threshold is scanned.

title.en: Keep the mobile plan invoice in the business name

moves.effect: Deductible = cost - min(50% x cost, ₪1,380/year); VAT reclaimable at 2/3 on a tax invoice in the business name.

title.he: לשלם הוצאות עסק באמצעי תשלום מתועד
